newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks set third straight record close.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks set third straight record close.

text.p: Toronto stocks nudged up to post their third consecutive record high close on Monday, powered by strength in 10 of the Toronto Stock Exchange's 14 sub-sectors.

The TSE's key 300 Composite index rose 13.20 points to a record high 6639.60 on volume of 84.9 million shares worth C$1.3 billion ($949 million). Advancing stocks outnumbered decliners 516 to 477, with 289 issues unchanged.
"The underlying tone of the market looks pretty good, particularly in Canada," said John Ing, President of Maison Placements Canada Inc. "A lot of the action was relegated to more technical factors."
Ing said some options expiries may have fueled buying in North American stocks, lifting strong interest-sensitive stocks such as banks and other financial services.
Gold and precious metals continued to slide.
The Toronto actives list was topped by Cara Operations Ltd., whose class A shares rose 0.05 to 5.65.

CanWest Global Communications Corp. rose 0.40 to 24.30. CanWest Chairman Israel Asper said on Monday he was handing the leadership reins at the Winnipeg-based television broadcaster to new President and Chief Executive Peter Viner, but that he would remain chairman.
Gold stocks lost more ground as Comex prices failed to rebound further in New York after last week's bounce off 12-year lows.
One trader said major Canadian gold producers had likely rallied as far as possible and might now face selling.

"Barrick (Gold Corp.) and Placer (Dome Inc.) are probably up to where they could run into resistance at any time, because I don't think the down(trend) is (over). So for traders, you maybe want to be very nimble and want to be taking profits at this point," the trader said.
Barrick fell 0.90 to 29.65, while Placer was also off 0.90 to 20.30.
